The `camel-sanitizer` module is a checker for development and tests. It watches the calls of the steps of the routes
of a running Camel application and reports, when it happens, that a processor breaks the contract of `AsyncProcessor`
-(a callback called twice, or a processor that throws instead of calling its callback), or that the commit of a consumer
+(a callback called twice, a processor that throws instead of calling its callback, or one that returns a value other
+than the one its callback is called with), or that the commit of a consumer
runs twice, never, or with the outcome of another exchange. It also warns about a step whose callback has not come. It
checks the code of Camel users as much as Camel's own: a custom `AsyncProcessor`, the producer or the consumer of a
custom component, a bean. A test that runs a broken path fails with a report that names the step and the class.

report still counts the calls of steps), so a report of R2 can name the step that handed a commit over.
+=== R3: one thread at a time
+An exchange can move between threads, but it is never used by two threads at the same time. This version checks the
+first part of the rule: the contract of `AsyncProcessor` at the call of each step. The value the callback of a call is
+called with (`doneSync`) must be the value `process(exchange, callback)` returns, and `true` means that the callback
+was called already, on the calling thread. A caller that uses the return value
+continues the exchange when `process` returns `true`, and leaves it to the callback when it returns `false`; a
+processor that returns the other value lets two threads continue the same exchange, or none. Most callers in Camel go
+on through the callback and do not use the return value, so in a route the mismatch is usually harmless today; it still
+breaks the contract, and the same processor breaks under a caller that uses it. It reports:
+* *process returned true, and its callback was called on another thread* (`RETURNED_TRUE_CALLBACK_ON_OTHER_THREAD`):
+the processor handed the exchange to another thread, which called the callback, and then returned `true` as if it had
+done the work itself (such as a processor that waits for its worker). With `false` the caller and that thread can both
+continue the exchange; with `true` that thread continued it while `process` still ran. The report has the thread and
+stack of the callback, and the return.
+* *process returned true before its callback was called* (`RETURNED_TRUE_BEFORE_CALLBACK`): `process` returned `true`,
+and the callback then came on another thread, or with `true`. The caller went on before the work of the processor was
+done.
+* *process returned false, and its callback was called with true* (`RETURNED_FALSE_CALLBACK_TRUE`): in either order,
+on any thread.
+The contract allows one case where the two values differ, and it is not reported: a processor that hands its callback
+to the reactive executor returns the value of the processor it calls, and the reactive executor then calls the callback
+with `false` on the calling thread, at once or after the work that thread is running. The channel of a step without an
+error handler does this, so a step that calls such a channel directly sees it: for example a `choice` whose branch has
+one step, in a route with `noErrorHandler()`.
+So a callback with `false` on the thread that called `process` is never reported, whatever `process` returns and
+whether it comes before or after the return. The check relies on the default reactive executor of camel-core, which
+runs a callback on the thread that scheduled it.
+Only the first call of the callback is compared (a second call is R1), and a call whose `process` threw is not
+compared (R1 reports it). The check is at the processor of each step, below its error handler, as R1 is; the channel of
+a step always continues the exchange through the reactive executor, so the value it returns itself says nothing and is
+not checked. It costs little: a small record per call, and a stack only for a callback on another thread before the
+return, or when a violation is reported. It is on by default, also with profile `dev`.
+A report of R3 looks like this:
+[source,text]
+Exchange sanitizer: process returned true, and its callback was called on another thread (R3)
+  exchange 5A1B...-0000000000000001, route prices, step lookup, processor com.acme.PriceLookup
+  the callback was called with false: thread price-worker-2
+      at com.acme.PriceLookup.lambda$process$0(PriceLookup.java:38)
+  then process returned true: thread Camel (camel-1) thread #3 - timer://prices
+      at org.apache.camel.support.StepHelper.process(StepHelper.java:63)
+      at org.apache.camel.processor.errorhandler.RedeliveryErrorHandler.processOutput(RedeliveryErrorHandler.java:266)
+  process(exchange, callback) must return the value its callback is called with (see AsyncProcessor).

+  Usual fix: when the work goes on another thread, return false from process and let that thread call the callback with false; return true only after the callback was called with true on the calling thread.
+The second part of R3, a short watch window at sampled points where a thread waits for another one that uses the same
+exchange, is not in this version.
